origin: a live research session raised a deep-dive finding as a compressed read-out of the report's code — four source snippets, a position at implementation depth, no question — and the user could not tell what was being asked; retold as a product scenario with three end states and one question, it was answered in a sentence. Every walk case until this one used a product-shaped report, so the corpus could not see the drift. The report here is fixture-authored in code on purpose: a product fork the user owns, hidden under three mechanisms, so what the raise translates and what it leaves in the record are both checkable
answers: y — yes, work through them now
conduct: The user returns to the relevance-measurement research after a day away. They remember a deep dive was running when they left and want to hear what it found before doing anything else. They run the shop, not the search stack: they know what a bad result page costs them and have opinions about which shoppers matter, and they do not know what a slice guard or a feature flag is. They opt in when offered and read the first raised finding with interest — but the walk stops before they answer. They volunteer nothing new and do not steer the conversation anywhere else.
